residencyRequirements.description: The plaintiff must have been a resident of North Dakota for at least six months before the commencement of the action.

waitingPeriod.description: North Dakota has no mandatory waiting period.

noFault.name: Irreconcilable Differences
noFault.description: Irreconcilable differences have caused the irremediable breakdown of the marriage

fault.name: Willful Neglect
fault.description: Willful neglect to provide the common necessities of life

fault.name: Conviction of a Felony
fault.description: Conviction of a felony after the marriage

fault.name: Insanity
fault.description: Insanity for a period of five years with confinement in a state institution

groundsForDissolution.notes: North Dakota allows both fault and no-fault grounds. Irreconcilable differences is the most common ground.

propertyDivision.description: North Dakota follows equitable distribution. The court divides all property of the parties, whether acquired before or during the marriage, in a just and equitable manner. The court considers the respective ages, earning abilities, duration of the marriage, conduct, station in life, and circumstances and necessities of each party.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: North Dakota does not strictly distinguish between marital and separate property. All property is subject to distribution, though the court considers how and when it was acquired.

legalCitations.description: Grounds for divorce — irreconcilable differences and fault grounds
Property division — equitable distribution of all property
Custody — primary residential responsibility and decision-making responsibility; parenting time

filingFees.notes: North Dakota filing fee for a divorce complaint is $160. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals.

basic.name: Financial Statement
basic.description: Mandatory disclosure of income, assets, and debts

basic.name: Judgment
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage (Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law, and Order for Judgment)

service.name: Summons
service.description: Formal service on defendant via sheriff or process server

service.name: Admission of Service
service.description: Defendant admits service and waives formal service
service.notes: Must be signed by defendant and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Parenting Plan
withChildren.description: Court order establishing residential responsibility, decision-making, and parenting time

withChildren.name: Child Support Obligation Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per North Dakota Child Support Guidelines (NDCC §14-09-09.7)

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per North Dakota Rules of Civil Procedure

inState.description: Defendant must file an answer within 21 days of service

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside North Dakota must file an answer within 21 days of service

childSupportGuidelines.description: North Dakota uses an income shares model. Both parents' net incomes are combined and child support is determined from the North Dakota Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would be unjust or inappropriate.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: North Dakota courts may award spousal support (not alimony) considering factors including the disadvantages of each party from the marriage, the ability of the supported spouse to engage in gainful employment, the financial needs and ability of each party, and the duration of the marriage.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Either party may request spousal support. The court has discretion to determine the amount and duration based on equitable principles.

court.name: District Court
court.description: Divorce is filed in the District Court in the county where either party resides.
